item.title: Trump jokes he'll move to Israel and become PM if Americans get 'tired' of him
item.description: In a lighthearted moment during a Fox News interview, Donald Trump playfully proposed his candidacy for the position of Israel's prime minister, citing a staggering 99 percent approval rating among Israelis. He went on to declare that by 2026, the US would cease its annual aid of $4 billion to Israel, sparking considerable debate over the implications for military support and relations, coinciding with the midterm elections unfolding in America.

item.title: Who protects those counting America's votes? US election workers face threats amid midterms
item.description: In response to escalating threats and harassment, local government workers overseeing elections in the US are now under heightened security measures. This includes installation of bulletproof glass and emergency panic buttons, alongside training to manage aggressive behavior and suspicious items. The situation is compounded by the departure of numerous election officials, complicating recruitment efforts. Federal authorities remain dedicated to investigating threats to maintain the integrity of the electoral process.

item.title: 77% of US voters fear AI election manipulation: Why deepfakes are raising alarm ahead of midterms
item.description: With the 2026 midterm elections approaching, generative artificial intelligence is finding its way into the political arena. This technology creates highly convincing fake materials, which blur the lines between fact and fiction for voters. Campaigns utilize machine-learning tools to personalize outreach, raising concerns about trust in media integrity and the electoral process. Research shows that many voters fear how AI-generated content may undermine the fairness of elections.

item.title: British wedding venue evacuated after workers uncover five World War II bombs while digging for solar panels; guests and residents forced to flee
item.description: While digging a trench at The Great Tythe Barn, workers stumbled upon five suspected World War II bombs, initially mistaking them for broken pipes. As their metal fins became visible, emergency services swiftly evacuated the area, setting up a 200-metre exclusion zone for safety. Identified as German explosives, the bombs were eventually neutralized in a controlled detonation, underscoring the historic shadows that still linger in various regions of Britain.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: MrBeast Funds Free School Lunches: Kansas teacher’s campaign sparks gift; families get relief
item.description: At Tonganoxie Middle School, agriculture teacher Beth Schartz took significant steps to address student lunch debt after a concerning incident involving unpaid lunch balances impacted a child. In a remarkable turn of events, YouTube sensation MrBeast stepped in, generously funding free lunches for the entire academic year. This initiative not only provided nourishing meals but also included free back-to-school clothing, positively impacting families and promoting inclusiveness in the school community.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Pennsylvania woman treated for breast cancer had rare lymphoma; court allows family's lawsuit
item.description: A Pennsylvania woman received breast cancer treatment for 13 months before doctors discovered she had a rare and aggressive lymphoma. She died in January 2019, and her family sued the treating oncologist, alleging that the delayed diagnosis reduced her chances of survival. After a trial court dismissed the case, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that a jury should hear the malpractice claim.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Arkansas man loses tax offset bid as court upholds ex-wife's $183,000 business share
item.description: Following their divorce in 2017, a couple in Arkansas found themselves embroiled in a lengthy legal dispute concerning their jointly owned business, Groundskeeper. Conflicts emerged regarding the business's valuation and tax obligations. The Arkansas Court of Appeals confirmed the wife's claim of $183,000, inclusive of prejudgment interest from the divorce date, mandating Craig Ballegeer to acquire his former wife's half-interest in the business.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Discarded Nets Become Hoops: Giannis foundation, Enaleia upcycle gear; 80 Athens courts benefit
item.description: In a remarkable initiative, the Charles Antetokounmpo Family Foundation and Enaleia have repurposed discarded fishing gear into vibrant basketball nets, enhancing public courts across Athens. This project not only replaces damaged nets but also tackles marine pollution by transforming waste into valuable resources for the community. Young athletes can engage with these recycled nets, fostering a sense of environmental awareness alongside their love for sports.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Purple 1888 Victorian house in LA listed for $2M
item.description: Listed at $2 million, the unique Esperanza House embodies 138 years of history as a Queen Anne Victorian masterpiece with a bold purple exterior. Previously owned by Leonora Pierotti Thomas, the house is rich in artistic character yet demands extensive restoration. Nonetheless, essential features like the pool remain functional, and the agent appeals to buyers keen on its historic value and future possibilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Georgia company loses appeal over $220,000 tax auction purchase as county claims sovereign immunity
item.description: Talon Assets, LLC acquired land in Atlanta for $220,000 at a county tax sale. Doubts about the property led them to request a refund and tax deed cancellation. However, Fulton County dismissed their case, invoking sovereign immunity as a legal defense. The Georgia Court of Appeals upheld this dismissal, leaving Talon's issues unresolved. This ruling highlights the challenges in pursuing financial claims against county governments in Georgia.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas farmers turn 640 acres of donated land into college scholarships for 300 students
item.description: A 640-acre farmland donation made to a Texas school district in 1984 has become a source of college scholarships for hundreds of students. Local farmers in Gruver volunteer their labour and equipment to grow crops, generating approximately $400,000 annually. Since 2016, the initiative has distributed nearly $3 million to around 300 students, helping them pursue higher education.
